source.title_on_document: Can Gen AI Improve Creativity in Students with Low Academic Performance? A Quasi-Experimental Study Based on Chinese Samples

supplement.where: Appendices A-C are included in the saved publisher article text at https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/21582440261449529. No separate external supplement is referenced. There is no local PDF; in_this_pdf=false does not mean the appendices are missing from the source text.
supplement.holds: Appendix A, Table A1: intervention and teacher scaffolding by condition. Appendix B, Table B1 and worked example: scoring rules. Appendix C, Table C1: Levene tests and degrees of freedom. The main Tables 2-3 contain creativity means, SDs, reported Ns, ANOVA tests and partial eta squares; the appendices add no standard errors or confidence intervals. Figure graphics are absent from the saved export.

paper_design_summary: In an Innovation Training course at a Shanghai secondary vocational school, 75 students in three intact classes received traditional project-based instruction with web search, ChatGLM with minimal teacher intervention, or ChatGLM with teacher structure support (Methods, Intervention Design and Participants; Appendix A, Table A1). Procedures explicitly states that classes were randomly assigned, although the authors call the design quasi-experimental; open-ended pre/post-tests were scored for fluency, originality, elaboration and flexibility (Methods, Procedures and Measurements). The post-test followed the intervention, but AI availability during the tests is not stated.

studies.label: Innovation Training: ChatGLM, teacher-supported ChatGLM, and traditional instruction

assignment.what_was_assigned: Three intact classes were assigned to instructional conditions in their ordinary course. This explicit class-level random assignment in Procedures is distinct from prior school assignment of students to classes described in Participants. The title and Limitations call the design quasi-experimental because it did not randomize individuals. Allocation sequence and concealment are not described.
assignment.quote: Three entire classes were randomly assigned to the control group, experimental group 1, and experimental group 2.
assignment.locator: Methods, Procedures, Phase I; Methods, Participants; Discussion, Limitations and Conclusion

arms.name: EG1: ChatGLM with minimal teacher intervention
arms.description: Students used ChatGLM for autonomous exploration, brainstorming, SWOT analysis, surveys, marketing and entrepreneurial plans, and presentation language. The teacher intervened little (Methods, Intervention Design; Appendix A, Table A1). N = 26 is printed in Participants and Table 2; assignment-stage people count is not separately given.

arms.name: EG2: ChatGLM with teacher structure support
arms.description: Students used ChatGLM with teacher support: clear task goals, task sheets, guiding questions, templates, process guidance and personalized feedback (Methods, Intervention Design; Appendix A, Table A1). N = 22 is printed in Participants and Table 2; assignment-stage people count is not separately given.

arms.name: CG: traditional project-based instruction with web search available
arms.description: Teacher-led project-based instruction without ChatGLM, using lectures, cases, group brainstorming, textbooks, online materials and traditional tools. Students had access to web search tools such as Internet Explorer (Methods, Intervention Design and Procedures, Phase I; Appendix A, Table A1). N = 27 is printed in Participants and Table 2; assignment-stage people count is not separately given.

participants.exclusions: No participant exclusions, attrition count or complete-case count is described. The reported analyzed count follows the total in Participants and Ns printed in Tables 2 and 4: EG1 = 26, EG2 = 22, CG = 27. Appendix C, Table C1 instead prints df1 = 2 and df2 = 51 for all creativity Levene tests, and df1 = 2 and df2 = 60 for psychological measures. These degrees of freedom do not agree with the stated sample sizes under the described analysis. No alternative people count is inferred, and the study is not labeled intention-to-treat.
participants.who: 11th-grade students aged 16 to 17 in the same Engineering major at a secondary vocational school in Shanghai. The three intact classes followed the same curriculum with the same teacher; the population is described as having low academic performance in the Chinese vocational education context (Methods, Participants).
participants.quote: A total of 75 11th-grade students from 3 intact classes in a secondary vocational school in Shanghai were selected for this study.
participants.locator: Methods, Participants; Tables 2 and 4 headers; Appendix C, Table C1

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGLM; specific model version not stated
ai_tool.how_used: Students used the conversational assistant during project-based learning for idea generation, SWOT analysis, surveys, marketing and entrepreneurial plans, and presentation language; EG2 added teacher structure support. The tool is described as based on a model trained by Zhipu AI Company and Tsinghua University KEG Lab (Methods, Intervention Design; Appendix A, Table A1). The interface figure is absent and no exact model version is stated.

task.description: The scored outputs are open-ended divergent-thinking test responses, not the classroom business plans. Pre-test: innovative strategies to make daily life more convenient. Post-test: innovative strategies to build an international child-friendly city in Shanghai. Tests draw on four ATTA dimensions without using its original questions. Training involves a business-plan project (Methods, Intervention Design and Measurements, Cognitive Tests for Creativity; Appendices A-B).
task.duration: Each test: 15 minutes. Study: 12 weeks, comprising preparation/pre-test (2 weeks), intervention (9 weeks, 90 minutes per week), and post-test (1 week) (Methods, Procedures and Measurements, Cognitive Tests for Creativity).

outcomes.name: Ability of fluency
outcomes.measure_detail: Two researchers scored pre/post-test responses; Appendix B describes two trained independent raters and discussion to resolve coding. Agreement coefficients are reported as higher than 0.76 (Methods, Measurements, Cognitive Tests for Creativity; Appendix B, Table B1 and coding procedure). These are manually coded counts summarized per participant. Number of distinct, relevant, non-repetitive ideas, with 1 point for each valid idea; irrelevant responses are excluded (Methods, Measurements, Cognitive Tests for Creativity; Appendix B, Table B1). Repeated-measures ANOVA examines time × group differences in participant scores. Table 2 omnibus interaction across all groups: F = 7.274, p = .002, partial η² = 0.222. The robustness LMM uses class as a random factor and reports F = 5.895, p < .01 for the overall interaction (Results, Creativity Test Results, paragraph preceding Table 2). This is the same outcome, not an additional outcome or pairwise contrast; no LMM coefficient, SE or CI is printed. The scored outcome is the post-test compared with a pre-test on a different scenario. Procedures, Phase III places the post-test after the intervention, but the source does not state whether ChatGLM was permitted or removed during testing, or the interval since last AI use. question, ai_available_when_produced and timing remain null rather than assuming with_ai or after_ai.
outcomes.delay: Post-test in Phase III (1 week), after intervention in Phase II (9 weeks); exact delay from last AI use and same-session versus later-session testing are not stated (Methods, Procedures).

Methods defines unusual responses as those given by less than 5% of the sample; Appendix B, Table B1 says no more than 5% of participants in the full sample, with 1 point per such idea. The worked example says ideas mentioned by ≤3 participants count as original. These source descriptions are preserved, not reconciled into an inferred threshold. This is participant originality, not across-people diversity. Repeated-measures ANOVA examines time × group differences in participant scores. The robustness LMM uses class as a random factor and reports F = 4.198, p < .05 for the overall interaction (Results, Creativity Test Results, paragraph preceding Table 2). The scored outcome is the post-test compared with a pre-test on a different scenario. sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: No participant reuse or overlap with another paper is reported; this source describes recruitment for the present study.

company_involvement.description: No company funding, author affiliation or participation in conducting the study is reported. Zhipu AI Company is named as a tool developer with Tsinghua University KEG Lab. Disclosed funding comes from public Chinese research programs, and the authors declare no potential conflicts of interest.

eligibility.reason: Methods, Procedures, Phase I explicitly reports random assignment of intact classes to the three conditions in ordinary coursework, supporting field_rct with class assignment despite the quasi-experimental label. Participants reports 75 students and Table 2 labels arms N = 26, 22 and 27, meeting the size criterion on printed counts; unexplained degrees of freedom in Appendix C, Table C1 are flagged. Open-ended test responses were scored by trained coders (Methods, Measurements, Cognitive Tests for Creativity; Appendix B, Table B1). Assignment to with_ai versus after_ai remains unresolved because test-time AI availability is unspecified; those outcome fields are null pending confirmation.

one_line_finding: Originality gains were greater with teacher-supported ChatGLM than with control (F = 12.058, p = .001, partial η² = .236), while independent ChatGLM showed no clear difference from control (F = 1.721, p = .199, partial η² = .051; Results, Table 3).
open_questions: Was ChatGLM permitted during the 15-minute creativity post-test, and what was the interval since last AI use? Procedures, Phase III does not establish AI withdrawal or exact timing; the export lacks the procedure figure graphics. question, ai_available_when_produced and timing are null rather than inferred.

What was the actual analyzed sample for each creativity outcome? Table 2 reports EG1 N = 26, EG2 N = 22 and CG N = 27, whereas Appendix C, Table C1 gives creativity df1 = 2 and df2 = 51; psychological tests give df2 = 60. No exclusions or missing observations are explained.

What procedure randomly assigned classes? Methods, Procedures explicitly reports class randomization, while the title and Discussion, Limitations and Conclusion call the study quasi-experimental. Sequence generation and concealment are unspecified.

Are class-adjusted pairwise estimates and uncertainty available? Results, Creativity Test Results gives LMM omnibus F tests and p thresholds with class as a random factor, but no pairwise class-adjusted coefficients, SEs or CIs; only three classes were assigned.

Which scoring rules were applied? Methods uses originality frequency less than 5%, while Appendix B, Table B1 says no more than 5%; elaboration counts detailed responses in Methods and the example, but detail instances in Table B1. Flexibility categories are described as pre-generated in Methods but determined during coding in Appendix B.
notes: Read the entire publisher text, including Appendices A-C, references and article metadata. No local PDF or page numbering is available, so locators use sections and tables. No figure values are extracted. Four output-scored outcomes are recorded; the source provides no overall-creativity composite or across-people diversity outcome. Learning attitude, flow experience, perceived creativity, self-efficacy and cognitive load are self-reports and excluded. Table 3 tests concern time × group interactions, not unadjusted post-test differences. Printed partial eta squares are retained; no effects or SEs are calculated. CG contrasts use ai_vs_active because web search and other materials were available. EG2 versus EG1 uses ai_design for teacher-supported versus minimally supported use of the same tool. Mixed structure denotes between-class treatment and within-student pre/post measurement. Assignment-stage people counts are not separately reported and remain null. Core eligibility follows reported assignment and Ns; the analyzed-count discrepancy and missing pairwise class-adjusted precision need audit before pooling. The supplement block identifies inline appendices present in the text, not a missing external file. Data availability statement offers data upon request to the corresponding author; no public data or code URL is supplied.
